subject: biology-2
question: A sea anemone shows **radial symmetry**, with body parts repeated around a central axis so that a slice along any plane through that axis yields mirror halves. It also has only two germ layers and is therefore **diploblastic**. To which phylum does this animal belong?
explanation: Cnidarians such as sea anemones and jellyfish are diploblastic and radially symmetric. Flatworms and annelids are triploblastic with bilateral symmetry, so B and C fail. Sponges have no true tissues or organized symmetry at all, which eliminates D.
